remaining_tasks.name: Fix event hooks on Windows (product gap, not a test gap)
remaining_tasks.summary: NEW FINDING, deliberately not fixed. hookScripts (electron/events/hooks.ts) selects on 'stat.mode & 0o111'. NTFS has no executable bit - Node reports 0o666 for a file written with mode 0o755 (verified by probe on 2026-10-09) - so hookScripts returns [] for EVERY file and event hooks do not run at all on Windows. Bypassing the filter is not enough: spawn(script) cannot execute a .sh on Windows without a shell. Fixing needs a product decision about how a Windows host invokes a hook (shebang, PATHEXT, or an explicit shell). Recorded in docs/WINDOWS-PORT.md under Risks, and pinned by two tests in electron/events/sources.test.ts that run on every platform.

decisions.decision: Capability probe (canCreateSymlink) rather than a process.platform === 'win32' check
decisions.rationale: A blanket Windows skip would silently drop coverage on the machines best placed to provide it - CI runners are administrators and CAN create symlinks. Probing means the 7 symlink tests RUN on windows-latest in CI and skip only on a developer laptop without Developer Mode. New helper: apps/desktop/electron/test-support/capabilities.ts.

decisions.decision: Fixed the 3 office/convert.test.ts failures in place instead of skipping them
decisions.rationale: sofficeCandidates and convertArgs are pure and are asked about other platforms; the failures were POSIX literals meeting Windows path semantics, not the code being wrong. Rebuilding the expectations with path.delimiter, path.join and pathToFileURL keeps every assertion on every platform. Net +2 tests in that file.

decisions.decision: Rewrote the bridge-plugin fake hermes from /bin/sh to Node
decisions.rationale: Paul's call. /bin/sh does not resolve from Node on Windows (ENOENT, verified), so a shell would have made these the only tests in the suite that could never run on the platform the port is for. The fake is now a generated .mjs invoked with process.execPath, and uses process.exitCode rather than process.exit so piped stdout flushes first. The 5 tests are now only gated on symlink capability.

decisions.decision: Did NOT weaken the package-io symlink security assertion
decisions.rationale: Per standing instruction. The assertion is unchanged and still rejects a symlinked asset. It is gated on the same capability probe, and a companion test was added that runs EVERYWHERE: replacing an asset with a directory exercises the same lstat(...).isFile() guard that defeats a symlink, so the security invariant is checked on every host. Net +1 test.

decisions.decision: C# native helper for Windows quick controls uses a JSON-lines protocol with a fixed-allowlist Protocol dispatcher and a FakeAudioController seam so tests do not need audio hardware
decisions.rationale: The C# helper exists in the same repo as the Node side. An allowlist is the only way to keep the boundary from becoming a general command runner. Default endpoint switching is deliberately excluded because Windows has no documented public API for it; the protocol returns not_supported for audio.default rather than rely on a private IPolicyConfig contract.
